verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI is documented as a library: the agent runs as "a plain object you call run() on" wherever you deploy it, and the vendor's Logfire platform is explicitly optional. Being model-agnostic, including OpenAI-compatible providers, avoids lock-in to any single model vendor. However, the evidence never states that agents can run fully self-hosted, for example with local or self-hosted models, so complete independence from external platforms is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of self-hosted or local model serving, an explicit open-source or self-hosting statement, and independent hands-on corroboration of fully on-prem deployment.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run my agents entirely on my own infrastructure with no dependence on the vendor's platform

citations.quote: The same agent runs everywhere you need it: behind a web frontend, in the terminal, on a voice call, on a durable background queue, or as a plain object you call run() on.
Pydantic AI has built-in (but optional) support for Logfire.
Pydantic AI is model-agnostic and has built-in support for multiple model providers
many providers are compatible with the OpenAI API, and can be used with OpenAIChatModel in Pydantic AI
